html:
The Cayuga, who call themselves Gayogo̱hó:nǫʼ, are one of the five original nations of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, living around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes of what is now New York. Odǫhwęja:deˀ is a Cayuga word for their land.

Their villages of longhouses stood among fields of maize, beans and squash. In the Confederacy they sat with the Oneida as the younger brothers, beside the Mohawk, Onondaga and Seneca.

Most Cayuga sided with Britain in the American Revolutionary War. In 1779 the Sullivan Expedition burned their towns and crops. Afterward many moved to the Six Nations reserve on the Grand River in Ontario, and others went west and ended up in Oklahoma. Only a small Cayuga Nation remains in New York.
